implementation.workflowContract: A single labeled search.many request projects Path, PatternId, LineNumber, Utf16Column and MatchText. Category comes from the pattern label, Origin comes only from an explicit caller-owned path manifest, and lexical evidence is not promoted to language-structure or runtime proof.
implementation.coverageContract: A diagnostic is proven covered only when non-comment declaration and emission findings occur under code origin and non-comment test and docs findings occur under their respective origins. Missing relations remain explicit.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,619 total tests, 1,585 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the new traceability test and Search suite also passed.
The separate review approved the lexical/provenance boundaries, missing-evidence behavior, escaping and fixture cleanup; tested source hashes, exact commands and the review artifact are retained.

The traceability fixture uses an independent expected occurrence map for all 14 labeled matches and asserts exact path/pattern cardinalities, comment handling and complete-versus-incomplete coverage; the registered semantic harnesses also passed.

The documented search.many projection compiles and runs against the traceability fixture, and the recipe documents that Origin is derived path-manifest provenance rather than an exposed Search column.

knownLimitations: Origin is derived from the caller-owned path manifest because the current search.many row schema does not expose an Origin column.
The recipe is lexical evidence aggregation; it does not parse language structure, resolve symbols, prove control flow or prove runtime test behavior.
A missing relation is meaningful only after the caller establishes a complete eligible path manifest and successful Search coverage.
